gaps.sentence: The chair on ___ the cat was sleeping was my grandmother's.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern for things; 'on where' and 'on that' are not grammatical.

gaps.sentence: We arrived at the hotel at noon, ___ the rooms were not ready.
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces non-defining clauses about time after a comma; 'that' is impossible after a comma.

gaps.sentence: This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which' and needs no preposition; 'the hotel which we stayed' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: My colleague Anna, ___ joined us in May, has already been promoted.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to Anna; non-defining clauses never use 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The restaurant ___ we had dinner last night has excellent reviews.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' after place nouns; no preposition appears in the clause.

gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The people ___ live upstairs are very quiet.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative for people.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.
